title: Euro Finance Week: AMLA Executive Board Member Derville Rowland holds roundtable with financial sector leaders

paras.text: In a fireside chat with Nickolas Reinhardt, Head of the EPIF Secretariat, Rowland set out how AMLA plans to deliver its regulatory mandates and how the private sector can prepare. She emphasised AMLA's commitment to trust and collaboration, recognising obliged entities as gatekeepers to the financial system.

Rowland explained that AMLA's technical standards and guidelines will follow a risk-based approach. They will set out stronger measures where risks are higher and simpler ones where risks are lower, while being mindful of compliance costs. The work draws on expertise from national supervisors, self-regulatory bodies and FIUs, as well as ongoing dialogue with industry through the Europe-wide AML/CFT community, roundtables, workshops, public consultations and hearings.

She also outlined AMLA's key deliverables for 2026, including technical standards on customer due diligence and group-wide policies, and guidelines on business-wide risk assessment, risk factors and ongoing monitoring.
Rowland concluded that the fight against money laundering is a collective effort, and that exchanges with the private sector continue to be essential to inform AMLA's work.
